decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Charizard Y. Charizard/Venusaur immediately overwrite sand with sun, threatening Excadrill with Heat Wave and Hippowdon with Solar Beam while Venusaur has Chlorophyll Sleep Powder pressure. Raichu covers Gyarados and provides Fake Out/Nuzzle tempo; Garchomp is the physical cleaner and pressures Excadrill, Blaziken, and opposing Rock-types.
decisions.notebook: Primary mode versus sand/Steel cores remains Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur, with Raichu for Gyarados/Electric tempo and Garchomp as a physical cleaner. Respect Hippowdon/Excadrill double Rock Slide, Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Mega Blaziken Speed Boost, and Gyarados Intimidate. Opponent Gengar carries Focus Sash; Whimsicott has Mental Herb.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blaziken. Lead Gyarados+Excadrill: Gyarados pivots turn 1 (Intimidate, EQ immunity, Heat Wave resist) while Excadrill Protects from Fake Out/Heat Wave/Sleep Powder; Hippowdon then re-enters to flip Drought back to sand, letting 280-speed Excadrill outrun even Chlorophyll Venusaur and OHKO Zard via Rock Slide. Mega Blaziken cleans Goodra-H/Raichu and abuses their sun vs Venusaur.
decisions.notebook: Opponent = Drought sun stack: Zard-Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur core, Raichu (Fake Out/Lightning Rod/Nuzzle) + Garchomp (Yache) mid, Primarina/Goodra-H slow back. KEY MECHANIC: Zard's mega Drought activates on its mega turn and overrides my lead sand — Hippowdon must RE-ENTER after the mega to flip weather back (switch-in Sand Stream beats established sun). Never leave Excadrill (sun Heat Wave OHKOs) or Hippowdon (sun Solar Beam ~OHKOs) exposed to Zard turn 1; Excadrill Protects. Excadrill at 280 in sand outruns their whole roster incl. Chlorophyll Venusaur (max 264); LO Rock Slide OHKOs Zard through spread reduction; Hippowdon Rock Slide also ~OHKOs Zard. Raichu's Electric moves cannot hit Hippowdon/Excadrill (Ground). CAUTION: Blaziken's Thunder Punch gets redirected by Raichu's Lightning Rod (Raichu immune, +1 SpA) — use CC/Flare Blitz when Raichu is adjacent or KO Raichu first. Venusaur: Focus Sash (needs 2 hits); Sleep Powder 75% hits everything I brought (Whimsicott is my only sleep-immune, benched game 1) — if sleep spam decides game 1, bring Whimsicott (Taunt stops powder via Prankster priority) in games 2-3. Garchomp: Yache halves first Ice Fang; Gyarados is the answer (EQ-immune, resists Dragon Claw, Intimidate); only Rock Slide hits Gyarados (2x). Goodra-H: Shell Armor (no crits); Body Press runs off its Def so Intimidate doesn't weaken it; Mega Blaziken CC OHKOs, Excadrill HH 2HKOs. Primarina: Excadrill Iron Head likely OHKOs; Blaziken TP only ~75-80% and Hydro Pump OHKOs Blaziken — don't rely on that line. Game 1 team: Gyarados+Excadrill lead, Hippowdon+Blaziken ba

decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard Y moves before Excadrill and sun-boosted spread Heat Wave guarantees its KO if it does not Protect. Venusaur Solar Beam guarantees Gyarados’s KO if it does not Protect; Focus Sash covers a faster Ice Fang. This forces their only strong answer into Protect/accuracy variance while preserving the primary sun mode.
decisions.notebook: Opponent lead Gyarados is Intimidate, Wacan Berry, Adamant; Excadrill is Life Orb, Adamant, Sand Rush. Continue prioritizing Mega Charizard Y plus Chlorophyll Venusaur against their sand/Steel mode; Raichu remains the Gyarados/Electric-tempo option and Garchomp a physical cleaner.

decisions.rationale: Sun Heat Wave is a guaranteed OHKO on Excadrill, so Protect is mandatory. Waterfall is sun-halved (33-76%, no KO) and Venusaur out-speeds in sun with 75% Sleep Powder, so attacking with Gyarados is a bad gamble. Double Protect wastes their powder/Heat Wave turn, keeps both my mons awake, and sets up turn 2: Hippowdon re-entry flips sand (Drought already active), restoring full-power Waterfall and letting Gyarados 133 outrun Venusaur 100-132.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur moves before both foes and Solar Beam cleanly threatens Gyarados before it can Waterfall or Ice Fang. Charizard is guaranteed faster than Excadrill and Heat Wave threatens its KO while still pressuring Gyarados. Their consecutive Protects are reduced-success gambles; attacking both slots maximizes the immediate double-KO outcome, with only Heat Wave accuracy as the main risk.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Gyarados: Intimidate, Wacan Berry, Adamant, Waterfall/Ice Fang/Dragon Dance/Protect. Excadrill: Life Orb, Adamant, Sand Rush, Rock Slide/Iron Head/High Horsepower/Protect. Opponent backline includes Sand Stream Hippowdon, Mega Blaziken, Prankster Mental Herb Whimsicott, and Focus Sash Gengar. Preserve Raichu for Electric tempo versus Gyarados and Garchomp as a cleaner; Charizard Y plus Chlorophyll Venusaur is the primary anti-sand mode.

decisions.rationale: Raichu preserves the stronger immediate tempo: next turn Fake Out can deny Sand Rush Excadrill while Venusaur pressures Hippowdon with Solar Beam, and Raichu remains the key Thunderbolt answer to Gyarados. Garchomp is slower than Sand Rush Excadrill and cannot safely apply its spread pressure beside Venusaur.

Switch resolves before moves: Hippowdon's Sand Stream overrides sun, disabling Chlorophyll (Venusaur drops to 100-132) and sun-boosted Heat Wave, while Sand Rush Excadrill hits 280 and moves first. LO Rock Slide at 4x OHKOs Charizard-Mega-Y even through spread; Venusaur's Sludge Bomb can't touch Excadrill, Solar Beam must charge in sand, and a sashed Venusaur dies to end-of-turn sand chip. Worst case (double Protect or Zard switch) still leaves sand up with Excadrill outspeeding their whole rost

decisions.rationale: Fake Out on Hippowdon is the only line that forces its Protect/Ice Fang off this turn and gives Solar Beam a clean guaranteed KO if Excadrill uses Rock Slide. Venusaur cannot be protected from both opposing attacks; this maximizes the chance to remove Sand Stream and restore a favorable Raichu/Garchomp endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has shown Hippowdon’s Sitrus Berry and Excadrill’s Life Orb Sand Rush Rock Slide/Protect. Against Hippowdon + Excadrill, prioritize removing Sand Stream when possible so Garchomp can outspeed Excadrill; preserve Raichu for Gyarados tempo.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Only Fake Out -> Excadrill delays it one turn, and Venusaur still dies turn 4 before acting since Excadrill (280) outspeeds and Fake Out is spent. If Fake Out hits Hippowdon instead, we lose Yawn but Venusaur still dies — good

decisions.rationale: Earthquake is the only listed offensive line that can remove Excadrill and meaningfully damage Hippowdon. Raichu Protect avoids taking its ally’s Earthquake and preserves it if Excadrill survives via Protect. Even moving second, trading Raichu’s tempo for Excadrill is the clearest route to a Garchomp endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Hippowdon has Sitrus Berry, Sand Stream, Rock Slide, Ice Fang, Yawn, Protect. Excadrill has Life Orb, Sand Rush, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Preserve Raichu when feasible for Gyarados tempo; versus sand, Garchomp must usually remove Excadrill before it can exploit its Speed.

decisions.rationale: 4v2 with Raichu unable to damage either Ground type. EQ is the only real threat and likely KOs Excadrill from 81%, so Protect scouts it while Ice Fang pops Yache and chunks Garchomp. No need to gamble a double-target coin flip or trade Excadrill for dead-weight Raichu. Next turn: HH + unhalved Ice Fang (42-74%) cleans Garchomp, or pivot Excadrill to EQ-immune Gyarados (Intimidate, 2x SE Waterfall) to preserve it.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]

decisions.rationale: Excadrill (280 Spe) moves first and guaranteed-KOs Raichu with HH (162-334%); Hippowdon Ice Fang 4x SE likely KOs Garchomp at 66% (42-74% range). If Garchomp Protects, Raichu dies and Excadrill HH KOs Chomp next turn; if Chomp EQs after Raichu faints, Hippo survives (neutral, Def 152) and finishes it. Raichu is fully walled by my Ground duo. Every branch wins.

Game is decided: Garchomp at 3% faints to Hippowdon's Ice Fang or to end-of-turn sand chip even through Protect or a Rock Slide flinch. Opponent has nothing left in back. Replacement choice is cosmetic; Blaziken enters.

reflections.summary: Lost because the Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun plan was poorly matched into Hippowdon+Excadrill: Hippowdon replaced sun with sand, Excadrill immediately threatened both leads, and the remaining Garchomp/Raichu endgame could not finish Hippowdon before Ice Fang removed Garchomp. Gyarados also remained untouched in back.
reflections.adjustment: Do not lead Charizard-Y/Venusaur into the revealed sand core. Lead Raichu+Garchomp next game to pressure or disrupt Excadrill immediately, and only bring Charizard-Y if it can be preserved until Hippowdon is weakened or removed.
reflections.notebook: Opponent used Hippowdon+Life Orb Sand Rush Excadrill as a sand mode; Hippowdon's Ice Fang is a major Garchomp check alongside Rock Slide/Yawn. Gyarados was held in back with Wacan Berry and may be their late-game win condition. Opponent brought Mega Blaziken in Game 1; Whimsicott and Gengar were not brought. Future plan: respect Hippowdon weather overwrite and avoid committing the sun lead into sand; prioritize early Excadrill control while keeping an answer for back Gyarados.

reflections.summary: Won on the strength of the Hippowdon+Excadrill sand core executing the preview plan: Hippowdon re-entry flipped Drought to sand on turn 2, LO Excadrill OHKO'd Mega Zard through spread Rock Slide, then removed Venusaur and Raichu with High Horsepower. Raichu was dead weight into two Grounds and Garchomp was forced to spam EQ around its own partner, while Hippowdon's Ice Fangs 2HKO'd Garchomp through Yache to close at 1% HP. The back-end plan failed despite the win: Mega Blaziken entered only as E
reflections.adjustment: Change the preview plan, not just the piloting: vs Zard-Y/Venusaur/Raichu/Garchomp, Mega Blaziken is a poor mega (EQ-weak, Thunder Punch Lightning Rod-bait) — bring Hippowdon/Excadrill/Gyarados/Whimsicott instead, with Whimsicott as Sleep Powder insurance and no reliance on the mega. In-game, when Excadrill falls, send Gyarados (EQ-immune, Intimidate) — never Blaziken — into Garchomp.
reflections.notebook: G1 WON via sand core; plan validated. Opponent = Drought sun stack: Zard-Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur, Raichu (Fake Out/Lightning Rod/Nuzzle) + Garchomp (Yache) mid, Primarina/Goodra-H slow back. G1 four: Zard/Venu/Raichu/Chomp; Sleep Powder never used — still expect it as their g2 adjustment (Venusaur lead to sleep Excadrill) or Primarina/Goodra-H brought. CONFIRMED DAMAGE: sand LO Rock Slide OHKOs Mega Zard through spread; HH OHKOs Raichu and KOs Venusaur; Hippo Ice Fang ~63% to Jolly Chomp, 2HKO once Yache eats the first hit. KEY MECHANICS: Zard mega Drought overrides lead sand — Hippowdon must re-enter post-mega to flip weather; never expose Excadrill/Hippowdon to Zard in sun. In sand Excadrill (280) outruns their roster. Raichu is zero-threat vs Ground duo — never trade a real mon for it; opponent will Protect Raichu and spam EQ rather than switch it. Excadrill at ~80% is inside Jolly Chomp spread-EQ range — Protect or pivot. TEAM PREVIEW LESSON: Mega Blaziken is a wasted slot vs this matchup (EQ-weak, Thunder Punch Lightning Rod-redirected) — g2 bring Hippowdon/Excadrill/Gyarados/Whimsicott; Gyarados (EQ-immune, Intimidate) is the correct Excadrill replacement into Garchomp. If Blaziken is ever in vs Raichu, use CC/Flare Blitz only. Venusaur Focus Sash; Whimsicott Prankster Taunt answers sleep spam. Solar Beam in sand = charge turn then half-power release. Goodra-H: Shell Armor; Mega Blaziken CC OHKOs, Excadrill HH 2HKOs. Primarina: Excadrill Iron Head likely OHKOs; Hydro Pump OHKOs Blaziken.
